chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Auditions and Carl Kress's role at the Onyx Club
summary: She auditioned around town; Carl Kress was a silent partner and Joe Helbock needed a singer.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But, the way things happen -- you know, they happen so fast. Getting back to the time when I finally got a chance to see Gladys and Claude -- Jennie's brother lived up on Sugar Hill. Lived at 409 Edgecombe Avenue.
So we finally got together. They arranged -- well I guess they -- you know, it takes time. So they came up to 409 which is around 155th Street and Edgecombe Avenue.
And I auditioned and every gin mill from 155th Street down to 52nd Street that day -- we went into clubs --

In fact, years later after I had been singing with the Kirby Band for a while and Billy Kyle -- you got Billy Kyle there -- Billy reminded me that he was one of the piano players that happened to be in one of the clubs that I auditioned and he played for me.
Claude didn't play -- everyone was there, and that got to be quite a thing.
But, when I got down to the Onyx Club, Joe Helbock -- as I said, before, was still out on the

west coast trying to get Stuff Smith back -- but Carl Kress --
The guitar player, he was a silent partner. And he was the one that heard me sing and he's the one that hired me.
And, of course, when Joe Helbock got back, he said he needed a singer like he needed a hole in his head.
So that's the reason I say, I didn't amount to very much until that article in the New Yorker came out.
